# Model risk management supervisory guidance (SR 11-7 / SR 26-2)

## Summary

SR 11-7 is the Federal Reserve's supervisory guidance on model risk management. It defines model risk as the potential for adverse consequences from decisions based on models that are incorrect or misused, and states it is manageable primarily through effective challenge: critical analysis by objective, competent, independent parties with the incentive to act. The full lifecycle is evidenced: model development, implementation and use (conceptual soundness, testing), validation (independence, ongoing monitoring, back-testing, outcomes analysis), and governance (board and senior management oversight, policies, model inventory, documentation).

SR 26-2 (Revised Guidance on Model Risk Management, April 2026, issued jointly with the OCC and FDIC) supersedes and replaces SR 11-7. It restates the model risk and effective challenge definitions, tailors applicability to banking organizations with more than $30 billion in total assets, emphasizes inherent risk and model purpose in proportionality, and adds vendor model coverage.

## Applicability

This note applies to organizations subject to US banking supervision that use models — including AI/ML models: SR 11-7's model definition covers any quantitative approach applying statistical, economic, financial or mathematical techniques, and machine-learning models are explicitly in scope. It is the supervisory anchor for the Brain's model validation, backtesting and monitoring notes.

## Governance Considerations

- Maintain a model inventory covering all models in use, including vendor and third-party models, with documented development, validation and monitoring status.
- Validate independently: validation must not report to model developers; effective challenge requires expertise, independence and incentives.
- Apply ongoing monitoring, back-testing and outcomes analysis after deployment (see [ai-model-backtesting](/concepts/ai-model-backtesting.md), [ai-model-monitoring](/concepts/ai-model-monitoring.md)).
- Board and senior management oversight, policies and documentation are supervisory expectations, not optional hygiene.
- Under SR 26-2, calibrate governance intensity to inherent risk and model purpose; track the supersession in policy documents.

## Limits

The phrase "three lines of defense" does not appear in the corpus and is not asserted. SR 11-7 is superseded: cite SR 26-2 for current supervisory expectations where applicable. Applicability to non-US organizations is a matter of adopted practice, not obligation. Both guidance texts carry extraction warnings in the technical quality control, mitigated by automated OCR-match verdicts on all flagged pages; human documentary review remains pending for those pages.
